result.title: Vision Models Capture Complementary Representations in Children That Converge in Adults
result.comment: 4 pages, 1 figure. Updated version of the CCN 2026 accepted abstract. Some analyses have been revised since presentation
result.summary: How the relationship between image-text aligned and vision-only models changes across development remains unknown. We applied time-resolved representational similarity analysis to EEG data from 8-year-olds, 12-year-olds, and adults. CLIP showed significant model-brain alignment already in children, whereas vision-only models aligned more strongly later in development. Residual analyses revealed complementary structure, with CLIP retaining alignment beyond an architecture-matched vision-only model from age 8. Much of the model-brain alignment reflected semantic structure, with EEG representations of category and animacy strengthening toward adulthood, while alignment with low-level image properties remained weak across age. Together, these findings suggest that image-text aligned and vision-only models capture complementary aspects of developing visual representations and may provide useful constraints for AI systems that aim to learn and adapt over time.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究用时间分辨的表征相似性分析（RSA）比较 8 岁、12 岁儿童与成人 EEG 同 CLIP 及纯视觉模型的对齐程度，并通过残差分析显示两类模型捕获互补的表示结构，语义维度（类别、生命性）随发育增强，低级图像属性对齐始终较弱。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「RSA 加残差分解」思路可能为核查 VLM 内部状态中语义与低级视觉信息如何互补共存提供分析工具，但该文研究的是人脑发育而非模型推理或 latent 状态生成，联系仅属可核查的推测。
